title: Error boundary exposes raw exception details in the renderer UI
reasoning: The fallback UI directly renders both error.toString() and error.stack. In a packaged desktop app, renderer exceptions can include local filesystem paths, internal implementation details, request URLs, or fragments of user-provided data. Showing that raw stack in the main user-facing UI broadens accidental disclosure beyond logs/dev tooling and can also make production failures more confusing for users.
recommendation: Render a generic production fallback and gate raw error details behind an explicit development-only condition or copy-to-report action that redacts sensitive values. Keep full details in controlled logs instead of the visible fallback.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and there is no evidence of a production/dev rendering assertion for ErrorBoundary.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a renderer test that throws under ErrorBoundary with a stack containing a fake local path or token-like value and asserts the production fallback does not render the raw stack while development mode can still expose diagnostics if intended.
minimumFixScope: Update ErrorBoundary fallback rendering and add one focused component test for the production-visible error UI.
